title: Roll a stored solar panel up onto its mounting stand
instruction: Tilt the solar panel up onto its stand.
context: Off-grid crews store panels flat on their mounting frames between seasons and re-angle them for the season - the tilt is the difference between a panel that charges and one that barely does. Adjusting a propped panel without carrying it off is the everyday version of this job.
setup: All rigid boxes on the station table (scene 'station', table top at 75 cm). A panel 9.8x18x1.5 cm, 120 g, dark blue-grey, lies flat with its centre at (27, -19) cm, rest + 8 cm: its far end (y -28 cm) on a storage post 2x3x8 cm, grey, centred (27, -29.5) cm, and its near end (y -10 cm) on the stand's crossbar 16x3x1.5 cm, grey, centred (27, -10.5) cm, rest + 8 cm, carried by two legs 2x3x6.5 cm at x 19/35 cm. A 1.5 mm toe lip 3.6x1.5 cm, grey, lies on the table with its face at y -26.25 cm, marking the seat ~1.3 cm behind the leaned panel's landing spot.
scoring: Scored at the episode end with the panel at rest (speeds under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s): 1.0 when the panel leans back on the crossbar at 25-35 degrees from horizontal, its bottom edge within 3 cm of the toe rail's face (y -26.25 cm), its face normal tilted toward the stand (the far edge up) and its yaw within 15 degrees of square; 0.5 for a 35-42 degree lean (overshot the seat); 0.0 flat, overturned, fallen, facing away, or propped anywhere else. Do-nothing: 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed; the panel spawns in one fixed layout on the post and crossbar.
fidelity: A rigid-body stand-in at bench scale. The roll-up is a real pivot about the crossbar's front edge inside a parallel-jaw pinch (the pad faces stay parallel to the panel's faces through the rotation); the seat is the geometric wedge a technician sets by eye. Panel electrical function is not simulated - the tilt and seat are exactly what a protractor and tape measure check.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2400 steps, active throughout, never landed the tilt); scripted demo: 1.0
